memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made all its utensils of bronze - its pots, shovels, sprinkling bowls, meat forks and firepans. They made a grating for the altar, a bronze network, to be under its ledge, halfway up the altar." - Exod 38:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pots, shovels, forks, firepans. This is the equipment of hard, dirty work.

We can romanticise Old Testament worship until we picture the reality. The altar was a place of blood, smoke, ash and heat. Priests carried away ashes with shovels. Someone had to clean it. Every day.

Worship in Israel was not primarily an aesthetic experience. It was physical, costly and messy — because sin is costly and messy.

That is worth remembering when our own service to God feels unglamorous. Someone has to handle the practical, thankless side of church life. Someone cleans up after the event. Someone deals with the difficult conversation nobody wants.

Notice the grating — a bronze network halfway up, letting air circulate so the fire could burn properly and ash could fall through. A hidden, functional detail that made the whole thing work.

There are people like that in every congregation. Nobody sees them; nothing functions without them.

Paul reminds us that whatever we do, whether in word or deed, we do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus (Col 3:17). Shovels included.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you avoid the unglamorous side of serving God?
2. Who does the "shovel work" in your church, and have you thanked them?
3. What practical need could you meet this week that no one would notice?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let me serve You in the messy and practical things, not only the pleasant ones. Amen.
